plan:
WHAT IT WILL TRADE: It joins a major leg of the day late, in the direction the leg is already running, takes the money off at the first look where the open profit is 2x ATR and at least $200 (roughly 25-40 points at 4 lots), and it refuses to go back in after a trade that didn't make that $200 — it has to wait for the next major move.

HOW IT TRIES TO BEAT THE CHAMPION: It isn't. This is not the champion's rule set and not the champion's days — it's the S line, seven new rules on a new brief, measured against a baseline that loses $20/day, and the declaration says in writing that it makes no dollar claim; the mechanism it is actually testing is churn — one trade per major move, and a jump back in only after a claimed profit with price still past that trade's best level, aiming to cut 17.6 trades a day down to 8 or fewer. So treat this as a behaviour run: it is trying to make the model trade like you, not to print a number above $624.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO HAPPEN: It would have to stop re-poking the tape within fifteen minutes of a losing exit and let the day's first three legs be the whole day's work — on the last S-line run the first three trades made +$1,988 and trades seven onward lost $4,080.

WHAT IT GIVES UP: It blocks good trades along with the bad — fifteen claims worth +$3,514 on the last run would have been refused — and by taking 25-40 points out of a 298-point median leg it will hold a smaller slice of each move than before.

BIGGEST RISK: The trade count falls exactly as designed and the money doesn't follow, and because the same run twice can differ by $324/day on nine days that were read while writing these rules, whatever dollar figure comes out won't settle it either way.

audit.raw:
VERDICT: GO

FAILING METRIC: $/day = −$20 (S1b baseline), i.e. $820 below the $800 bar — far further from its bar than side accuracy (0.818, passing) or capture (0.085, bar 0.15).

AIMED AT IT: PARTLY — S4 attacks the churn that funds the losses (15.2→≤8 trades/day, non-claim rebuys, patience) and pre-commits to making no dollar claim, so it aims at the *mechanism* behind $/day without being able to resolve $/day itself; its own cited trades net ≈0 (−$1,550 group A vs +$1,570 group C).

MEASURABLE: YES — the declared verdict is C1–C10 counts, not dollars, and those move far outside their own noise (trades/day 15.2/17.6 → mean ≤8 with ≥6 of 9 days ≤8; held ≤10 min 31/35% → ≤15%; non-claim median hold 15 → ≥25 min); the dollar reading is correctly fenced off as in-sample and inside the $324/day floor.

MISSING:
1. Reconcile the two gate-implied entry rates before the run: the labeller (verified today, `reports/recursive_loop/S4_label_replay.txt`) passes only 23/137 and 21/158 recorded entries = **2.3–2.6 entries/day**, against the change file's "the gate alone leaves 6.3–8.0/day". They measure different things (recorded entries classified vs. entries permitted), but C1's threshold and C3's floor were set off the higher number — record which is C1's expectation and that C3 (no day under 2 trades) is the live failure mode if S4 lands near 2.5/day.
2. Record the per-day MIL count for the nine days now (zero model cost, harness already tracks it): it is the ceiling on permitted "new major move" entries and therefore the denominator C1 and C3 are actually read against. Without it, a C1 pass cannot be told apart from a tape that simply had few major moves.
3. Pre-declare rule-7 format compliance as a reported count (share of reasons parsing `DAY:` / `BOOK:` / `NOW:`). H(iii)'s "rule not shown to bind" is unreadable if you cannot show the model was reading the page at all; C5/C6 only cover the gate label.

REASON: Four preflight rounds have already closed the real interpretive holes — the labeller replay is causal and runs, the dollar reading is pre-committed as unresolvable, C9 is split so scratching cannot pass it, C7/C8 are split by exit class, C1 carries a dispersion term, and the BRIEF_V3-plus-scorecard confound is stated rather than hidden. The remaining gap is a 2.5× unreconciled discrepancy in the one number that decides the run (C1/C3), which is cheap to record from artifacts already on disk and does not justify spending another cycle before launch.
